# Product Knowledge Base Standard

## 1. Purpose

One governed, version-controlled knowledge base per product that people and AI agents use to understand, build, change and run payments systems safely.

- It records **what is true about the product**, **who it serves**, **why it is built this way** and **how to run it**.
- It does not replace the SDLC. BMAD, Spec Kit, Jira or any process keeps its own working artifacts.
- Every fact has **one owner and one home**. Everything else links to it.

## 2. What it contains

| Area | Knowledge | ID | Owner |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product | Overview: vision, value, stakeholders, success measures, boundaries | `overview.md` | Product owner |
| Product | Personas: customers, operators, partners | `PER-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Customer and operator journeys (current and target) | `JRN-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Use cases | `UC-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Pain points with evidence, severity and resolution status | `PAIN-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Capabilities | `CAP-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Business rules | `BR-*` | Product owner |
| Product | Quality attributes: availability, latency, throughput, security, resilience targets | `NFR-*` | Product architect |
| Product | Data: key entities, classification, retention | `data/` | Product architect |
| Product | Compliance applicability: which obligations and controls apply | `compliance.md` | Product owner + compliance |
| Product | Glossary | `TERM-*` | Product owner |
| Architecture | C4 model: context, containers, components, deployment, key flows | `architecture/model/` | Product architect |
| Architecture | Architecture states: current, interim, target | `states.yaml` | Product architect |
| Architecture | Decisions | `ADR-*` | Product architect |
| Architecture | Narratives: security, resilience, integration, data flow | `NAR-*` | Product architect |
| Architecture | API and event contracts | OpenAPI / AsyncAPI beside the service | Service team |
| Operations | Runbooks, support model, incident learnings | `RB-*` | Operations lead |
| Quality | Test strategy, test data rules, rule-to-test traceability | `quality/` | QA lead |
| Agents | `AGENTS.md`, product skills, golden questions | — | Product architect |

Shared payments knowledge lives in the **domain tier**, not in products: rails, message formats and mappings, code sets, calendars, obligations (`OBL-PAY-*`), controls (`CTL-PAY-*`), approved patterns (`PAT-PAY-*`), domain glossary.

**Not stored here (linked instead):**

| Item | Lives in | How it connects |
|---|---|---|
| Roadmap and backlog, feature requests | Product management tool (Jira) | `product.yaml` links; epics cite `PAIN-*`, `UC-*`, `CAP-*` |
| Raw customer feedback, research notes, survey data | Research repository | Cited as evidence in `PAIN-*` and `JRN-*` |
| In-flight PRDs, epics, stories, specs | SDLC framework folders | Cite IDs; promoted at close |
| Deployments, incidents, tickets, runtime state | Systems of record | Queried through MCP |
| Secrets, customer or production data | Nowhere in the knowledge base | — |

## 3. Structure

Three tiers. Products reference upper tiers by ID and pinned version, never by copy.

| Tier | Repository | Holds |
|---|---|---|
| Enterprise | `enterprise-context` | This standard, schemas, AI and data policies, governance skills |
| Domain | `payments-domain-context` | Rails, message formats, code sets, obligations, controls, patterns, domain glossary and skills |
| Product | Each product repo | Everything product-specific (below) |

```
<product-repo>/
├── AGENTS.md                      short, human-verified agent instructions
├── product.yaml                   identity, owners, links (roadmap, backlog, research), domain pin, SDLC mapping
├── product-context/
│   ├── INDEX.md                   generated index of every artifact, never edited by hand
│   ├── overview.md                vision, value, stakeholders, success measures, boundaries
│   ├── personas/                  PER-*   customers, operators, partners
│   ├── journeys/                  JRN-*   customer and operator journeys, current and target
│   ├── use-cases/                 UC-*    what each persona does with the product
│   ├── pain-points/               PAIN-*  known problems, evidence, severity, resolution
│   ├── capabilities/              CAP-*   what the product does for the business
│   ├── business-rules/            BR-*    what must always be true
│   ├── quality-attributes/        NFR-*   availability, latency, throughput, security, resilience
│   ├── data/                      key entities, data classification, retention
│   ├── compliance.md              applicable obligations and controls (by domain ID)
│   └── glossary/                  TERM-*  product-only terms
├── architecture/
│   ├── model/                     C4 model, one file per state, plus states.yaml
│   ├── views/                     generated C4 diagrams, never hand-edited
│   ├── narratives/                NAR-*   security, resilience, integration, data flow
│   └── decisions/                 ADR-*
├── operations/
│   ├── runbooks/                  RB-*
│   ├── support-model.md           on-call, escalation, user-facing service levels
│   └── incident-learnings/        lessons promoted from post-incident reviews
├── quality/
│   └── test-strategy.md           approach, test data rules, rule-to-test traceability
├── evaluation/golden-questions.yaml
├── .agents/skills/                product skills
├── services/*/openapi.yaml …      contracts beside the code they describe
└── <SDLC folders, e.g. _bmad/, _bmad-output/>   owned by the SDLC framework
```

**How product knowledge links up:** persona → journey → use case → capability → business rule → C4 element → test. Pain points attach to the journeys, use cases or personas they affect, and to the epic that addresses them.

## 4. Core rules

1. **One source per fact.** Graph, search index, generated docs and agent memory are derived and rebuildable.
2. **Reference, don't copy.** Link by ID (`BR-PMTHUB-042`, `OBL-PAY-011`) instead of restating text.
3. **Front matter on every artifact:** `id`, `type`, `status`, `owner`, `review_by`, `provenance`, `relations`. CI, the catalog and the graph read it.
4. **Humans approve.** AI drafts as `status: proposed`. Only a CODEOWNER review makes it `active`.
5. **Live facts are queried**, never copied into files.
6. **`AGENTS.md` stays small:** commands, hard constraints, pointers. No generated overviews.
7. **Nothing sensitive:** synthetic examples only; no customer data, secrets or production messages. Pain-point evidence is summarized and linked, never pasted.
8. **Conflicts are reported, not resolved silently.** Precedence: regulation and policy → active rules and accepted ADRs → architecture baseline → in-flight SDLC artifacts → code → generated docs.

## 5. Architecture (C4)

- Architecture is described at C4 levels: **system context**, **containers**, **components** (only where they explain a decision), **deployment**, and **dynamic views** for critical payment flows.
- It is kept as **one model**, not hand-drawn diagrams. All C4 diagrams in `views/` are generated from it.
- The department stores the model in **FINOS CALM** format. CALM adds machine-checkable controls and approved patterns. Conventions: [Reference: CALM Conventions (payments department)](#reference-calm-conventions-payments-department).
- Model elements link to rules (`BR-*`), decisions (`ADR-*`), quality attributes (`NFR-*`) and controls (`CTL-PAY-*`) by ID.
- Element IDs match catalog names and stay the same in every state.

## 6. Current, interim and target state

| State | Meaning | Changes when |
|---|---|---|
| **Current** | What runs in production today | A release goes live |
| **Interim** | A planned intermediate step: coexistence, bridge, parallel run | Its plan changes; removed after it goes live |
| **Target** | The approved end state | An ADR changes the target |

Rules:
- Each state is one architecture model file; `states.yaml` lists them in order with status (`live`, `planned`, `retired`), planned window, delivering epics, approving ADRs and exit criteria.
- Exactly one current state. Interim and target exist only when they differ from current.
- Temporary elements (bridges, adapters, dual writes) are marked transitional, with a sunset date and the ADR that allows them.
- Journeys, rules, ADRs and runbooks describe the current state by default. Future-only knowledge sets `state: target` or `state: transition-NN` and a future `effective_from`. A target journey is the customer view of the target architecture.
- **At go-live:** the delivered state becomes current, `states.yaml` is updated, target journeys that are now live become current, transitional runbooks are activated or retired. Git keeps history.

Which state to use:

| Task | Read |
|---|---|
| How does it work? Troubleshooting, operations | Current |
| Implement a slice | Diff: current → the interim state that slice delivers |
| Design, roadmap, new epic | Target, plus the next interim state, target journeys, open pain points |
| Audit, impact of a regulation change | Current, then target |

Scenarios: a **stable product** has current only; a **greenfield product** has target only until first release; a **modernization** has current, one or more interim states, and target.

## 7. Using it with BMAD

| BMAD step | Knowledge base role |
|---|---|
| Analysis, product brief | Reads overview, personas, journeys, open pain points. Cites `PAIN-*` and `JRN-*` as the problem. |
| PRD | Reads use cases, capabilities, business rules, NFRs, obligations. Cites IDs, never restates. |
| Architecture | Reads current and target C4 model, ADRs, domain patterns. Proposes a new interim or target model plus ADRs. |
| Readiness gate | No contradiction with active rules, accepted ADRs, NFRs or obligations; model validation passes. |
| Stories | Acceptance criteria cite `BR-*`, `NFR-*` and `ADR-*` IDs. |
| Retrospective | **Promotion:** new or changed rules, ADRs, use cases, journeys, runbooks via PR; pain points marked resolved; or an explicit "none". |
| Release go-live | Delivered state becomes current. |
| After promotion | Archive completed epics and stories so agents don't treat them as current requirements. |

- BMAD's own project-context block in `AGENTS.md` stays in its marked section. Neither tool edits the other.
- Configure BMAD through its supported customization mechanism, not by editing core files.
- Details: [Reference: SDLC Framework Integration (BMAD first, then others)](#reference-sdlc-framework-integration-bmad-first-then-others).

## 8. Using it without BMAD

The same four touchpoints apply to any process (Jira epics, Spec Kit, Scrum):

1. **Before design:** read the baseline (pain points, journeys, current and target architecture, rules, ADRs).
2. **Before build:** run the same readiness check.
3. **At epic or feature close:** run promotion.
4. **At go-live:** update states.

Record the process and its artifact locations under `sdlc:` in `product.yaml`.

## 9. Keeping it current

| Trigger | Action | Owner |
|---|---|---|
| Every PR | CI: validator, model validation, secret scan, regenerate `INDEX.md` and C4 views | Automated |
| Epic or feature close | Promotion PR (or "none") | Product architect |
| Release go-live | Promote state to current; update journeys and runbooks | Product architect + ops |
| Customer research, complaints, ops feedback | Add or update `PAIN-*` with linked evidence | Product owner |
| Incident | Update runbook; record the learning; check rules, NFRs and ADRs involved | Operations lead |
| Scheme or regulation change | Domain release; products upgrade their pin and review impact | Domain architect + compliance |
| `review_by` reached | Review, re-date, deprecate or supersede | Artifact owner |
| Quarterly | Scorecard and golden-question run; fix the lowest scores | Product architect |

Stale knowledge is a defect: overdue obligations fail CI; other overdue artifacts warn.

## 10. How agents use it

1. Start at `AGENTS.md` → `product.yaml` → `product-context/INDEX.md`.
2. Pick the architecture state for the task (section 6).
3. Retrieve by ID and path first; use catalog or graph for relationships; MCP for live state; search only for unstructured history.
4. Read `active` artifacts by default. Ignore `superseded`, `deprecated` and `retired` unless the task is historical.
5. Cite IDs for every business, regulatory or architectural claim.
6. Draft new knowledge as `proposed`; never mark it `active`.

## 11. Operating modes (for agents running this skill)

- **A. Assess** (read-only): inventory existing knowledge, owners, duplicates, gaps; run the validator; write `context-assessment.md` with the scorecard from [Reference: Quality, Evaluation and Rollout](#reference-quality-evaluation-and-rollout).
- **B. Bootstrap:** after A, create `product.yaml`, folders, `AGENTS.md`, overview, personas, journeys, pain points, the current C4 model and key rules from evidence (docs → research → contracts → code), all `proposed`; add the golden-question set; open a PR.
- **C. Map an SDLC framework:** fill `sdlc:` in `product.yaml`; wire the four touchpoints in section 8.
- **D. Promote:** extract candidates from a finished epic or release; update existing artifacts before creating new ones; PR using `templates/promotion-checklist.md`.
- **E. Audit:** run `scripts/validate_context.py`; check model-to-code drift and rule-to-test coverage on a sample; report blockers first.
- **F. Evaluate:** run the golden questions; track retrieval accuracy, correctness and stale-source hits over time.

## Reference: Repository Layout

Adapt names to existing conventions. What matters is that each knowledge type has exactly
one home and that the home is discoverable from `product.yaml`.

### 1. Enterprise tier (one repo, bank-wide)

```
enterprise-context/
├── standard/                 # this standard: schemas, ID conventions, status model
│   ├── schemas/              # JSON Schema for front matter per artifact type
│   └── id-conventions.md
├── policies/                 # AI usage, data handling, secure coding (or links to the policy system of record)
├── skills/                   # bank-wide governance, security, standards skills (curated)
├── agents/                   # shared subagent definitions
└── CODEOWNERS
```

### 2. Domain tier (one repo for payments)

```
payments-domain-context/
├── domain.yaml               # domain id, version, owners, release notes
├── glossary/                 # one file per term, or glossary.yaml
├── rails/
│   ├── fedwire/              # scheme rules summary, cut-offs, message set, limits
│   ├── chips/
│   ├── ach/
│   ├── rtp/
│   ├── fednow/
│   └── swift/
├── messages/
│   ├── catalog.yaml          # message types and versions in use per rail
│   ├── mappings/             # internal canonical model <-> rail message formats
│   └── code-sets/            # status, reason and return codes
├── calendars/                # holiday calendars and cut-off definitions (or pointer to the system of record)
├── obligations/              # regulatory and scheme obligation register (OBL-*)
├── controls/                 # control catalog mapping (CTL-*) or pointer to GRC system
├── rules/                    # cross-product business rules (BR-PAY-*)
├── patterns/                 # approved architecture patterns (PAT-PAY-*: idempotency, saga, reconciliation ...)
├── models/                   # architecture model assets (CALM format)
│   ├── patterns/             # machine-checkable versions of PAT-PAY patterns
│   ├── controls/             # CTL-PAY-*.requirement.json control requirement definitions
│   └── shared-nodes/         # rails, sanctions screening, funds control and other shared systems
├── decisions/                # domain-level ADRs
├── skills/                   # reusable payments skills
└── CODEOWNERS
```

Release the domain repo with semantic versions. Products pin a version in `product.yaml`
and upgrade deliberately, so a scheme-rule change is a visible, reviewable event.

### 3. Product tier (each product repo, or a product-context repo for multi-repo products)

```
<product-repo>/
├── AGENTS.md                         # small, human-verified; see template
├── CLAUDE.md                         # optional adapter: "@AGENTS.md" plus Claude-only notes
├── .github/copilot-instructions.md   # optional adapter pointing to AGENTS.md
├── product.yaml                      # identity, owners, links (roadmap, backlog, research), domain pin, SDLC mapping
├── catalog-info.yaml                 # catalog descriptor (e.g. Backstage), if a catalog is used
├── product-context/
│   ├── INDEX.md                      # GENERATED by validate_context.py; do not edit
│   ├── overview.md                   # vision, value, stakeholders, success measures, boundaries
│   ├── personas/                     # PER-*  customers, operators, partners
│   ├── journeys/                     # JRN-*  customer and operator journeys (state: current or target)
│   ├── use-cases/                    # UC-*   what each persona does with the product
│   ├── pain-points/                  # PAIN-* known problems, evidence links, severity, resolution
│   ├── capabilities/                 # CAP-*
│   ├── business-rules/               # BR-<PRODUCT>-*
│   ├── quality-attributes/           # NFR-*  availability, latency, throughput, security, resilience
│   ├── data/                         # key entities, data classification, retention
│   ├── compliance.md                 # applicable OBL-PAY-* and CTL-PAY-* with product notes
│   └── glossary/                     # product-only terms; domain terms are referenced, not copied
├── architecture/
│   ├── model/                        # C4 model, one file per state (current / transition-NN / target) + states.yaml
│   ├── views/                        # GENERATED C4 diagrams; never hand-edited
│   ├── narratives/                   # NAR-* security, resilience, integration, data flow
│   └── decisions/                    # ADR-*
├── operations/
│   ├── runbooks/                     # RB-* runbooks, reconciliation and recovery procedures
│   ├── support-model.md              # on-call, escalation, user-facing service levels
│   └── incident-learnings/           # lessons promoted from post-incident reviews
├── quality/
│   └── test-strategy.md              # approach, test data rules, rule-to-test traceability
├── evaluation/
│   └── golden-questions.yaml
├── .agents/skills/                   # canonical product skills (cross-tool location)
├── .claude/skills/                   # symlinks or synced copies for Claude Code, if used
├── <SDLC framework folders>          # e.g. _bmad/, _bmad-output/ — owned by the framework
├── services/ … src/ … tests/ …       # code, with OpenAPI/AsyncAPI contracts beside each service
└── CODEOWNERS                        # product-context/, architecture/, operations/ require owner review
```

#### Product discovery knowledge and what stays outside

- Personas, journeys, use cases and pain points are **durable** product knowledge: they describe
  who the product serves and what hurts today, and every PRD or epic cites them by ID.
- Raw research (interview notes, survey data, complaints, recordings) stays in the research
  repository; `PAIN-*` and `JRN-*` summarize it and link to it as evidence.
- Roadmap, backlog and feature requests stay in the product management tool; `product.yaml`
  links to them, and epics cite the `PAIN-*`, `UC-*` and `CAP-*` they address.

#### Where contracts live

OpenAPI and AsyncAPI documents live with the service that owns the contract (for example
`services/payment-api/openapi.yaml`). The product context links to them by path or catalog
reference. Do not keep a separate `knowledge/APIs/` copy.

#### Multi-repo products

If a product spans several repos, create one `<product>-context` repo that holds
`product.yaml`, `product-context/`, `architecture/` and `operations/`. Each service repo keeps
its own small `AGENTS.md` that points to the product context repo and its own contracts.

### 4. Skills location and adapters

- Keep one canonical copy per tier. For repos, `.agents/skills/` is the emerging cross-tool
  project location (read by Codex, Cursor, Copilot and others). Claude Code reads
  `.claude/skills/`, Copilot also reads `.github/skills/`. Sync or symlink from the canonical
  folder; never maintain divergent copies.
- Enterprise and domain skills are installed from their repos (pinned version), not pasted in.
- Vendor instruction files (`CLAUDE.md`, `copilot-instructions.md`) are adapters that point to
  `AGENTS.md`. They never hold product knowledge.

### 5. Shared ownership of AGENTS.md

`AGENTS.md` can have several writers: humans, this standard, and SDLC tooling (current BMAD
releases write a verified project-context block into it). Use clearly delimited sections:

```
<!-- BEGIN product-context (owner: product architect) -->
...
<!-- END product-context -->

<!-- BEGIN bmad-project-context (owner: BMAD) -->
...
<!-- END bmad-project-context -->
```

No tool edits outside its own markers. The validator warns if the file grows beyond the
configured line budget (default 150 lines).

### 6. Things that are deliberately not here

- A generic `knowledge/` bucket. It becomes a second home for everything.
- Copies of domain rules, message mappings or regulations in product repos.
- Completed PRDs, epics and stories left in active planning folders.
- Rendered diagrams that are edited by hand.

## Reference: Artifact Schemas

Every durable artifact is a Markdown file with YAML front matter. The front matter is the
contract that the validator, catalog, graph and indexes read. The body is for humans and
agents. Keep one concept per file so each can be addressed, reviewed and superseded alone.

### 1. ID conventions

Format: `<TYPE>-<SCOPE>-<NNN>` where `SCOPE` is the product code (2 to 10 uppercase letters or
digits) or `PAY` for the payments domain tier, and `NNN` is at least three digits.

| Prefix | Artifact | Typical home |
|---|---|---|
| `PER` | Persona (customer, operator, partner) | product `product-context/personas/` |
| `JRN` | Customer or operator journey | product `product-context/journeys/` |
| `UC` | Use case | product `product-context/use-cases/` |
| `PAIN` | Pain point | product `product-context/pain-points/` |
| `CAP` | Capability | product `product-context/capabilities/` |
| `BR` | Business rule | product `product-context/business-rules/` or domain `rules/` |
| `ADR` | Architecture decision record | `architecture/decisions/` (product or domain) |
| `NFR` | Quality attribute (availability, latency, throughput, security, resilience) | product `product-context/quality-attributes/` |
| `TERM` | Glossary term | `glossary/` |
| `RB` | Runbook / operational procedure | product `operations/runbooks/` |
| `OBL` | Regulatory or scheme obligation | domain `obligations/` |
| `CTL` | Control (or pointer to GRC control) | domain `controls/` |
| `PAT` | Approved architecture pattern | domain `patterns/` |
| `NAR` | Architecture narrative | `architecture/narratives/` |

Examples: `BR-PMTHUB-042`, `ADR-PMTHUB-024`, `OBL-PAY-007`, `TERM-PAY-015`.

Rules:
- IDs are permanent. Never reuse or renumber. A changed rule gets a new version, or a new ID that supersedes the old one when its meaning changes.
- Systems, components, APIs and teams use catalog entity references, not these IDs (for example `component:payment-api`, `api:payment-api-v2`, `team:payments-hub`).
- File name = `<ID>-<short-slug>.md` so humans and agents can find it by either.

### 2. Common front matter (all types)

```yaml
---
id: BR-PMTHUB-042
type: business-rule          # persona | journey | use-case | pain-point | capability | business-rule
                             # | quality-attribute | adr | glossary-term | runbook
                             # | obligation | control | pattern | narrative
title: Counterparty validation before RTP authorization
status: active               # proposed | active | deprecated | superseded | retired
owner: team:payments-hub     # must resolve to a CODEOWNERS team
version: 3                   # integer, bump on any meaning change
review_by: 2027-03-31        # next scheduled review (see cadence table)
classification: internal     # public | internal | confidential ; "restricted" is not allowed in the context layer
supersedes: [BR-PMTHUB-017]  # optional
superseded_by:               # required when status is superseded
provenance:
  method: human              # human | ai-draft | extracted
  sources:                   # evidence: paths, contract files, PRs, policy references
    - product-context/prd-archive/epic-12.md
  verified_by: jdoe          # required when method is ai-draft or extracted and status is active
  verified_at: 2026-09-20
relations:                   # controlled vocabulary, see section 4
  implements: [CAP-PMTHUB-003]
  governed_by: [OBL-PAY-011]
  applies_to: [component:rtp-gateway]
tags: [rtp, validation]
state: current               # optional: current (default) | transition-NN | target
---
```

`state` marks knowledge that applies only to a future architecture state. Pair it with a future
`effective_from`. When that state goes live, set `state: current` (or remove the field).

### 3. Type-specific fields and body sections

#### Persona (`persona`)

Body: who they are, goals, context of use, channels, what success looks like for them.
No real customer names or data; personas are archetypes.

#### Journey (`journey`)

Additional front matter: `persona` (a `PER-*`), `state` (`current` default, or `target`).
Body: numbered stages; for each: what the persona does, touchpoint or channel, system behaviour
(C4 element IDs), and pain points (`PAIN-*`). A target journey states which ADR or state delivers it.

#### Use case (`use-case`)

Additional front matter: `persona`. Relations: `implements` → `CAP-*`, `depends_on` → `BR-*`.
Body: goal, trigger, preconditions, main flow, alternate and failure flows, postconditions.

#### Pain point (`pain-point`)

Additional front matter:
```yaml
severity: high               # low | medium | high | critical
resolution: open             # open | planned | mitigated | resolved
evidence:                    # links to research, incidents, complaints, metrics (never pasted content)
  - <link>
```
Relations: `affects` → `JRN-*`, `UC-*`, `PER-*`; `related_sdlc` → the epic that addresses it.
Body: the problem in the persona's words (summarized), impact (time, cost, risk, customer effect),
frequency, current workaround. When the fix goes live set `resolution: resolved`.

#### Quality attribute (`quality-attribute`)

Additional front matter: `measure` (e.g. "p99 end-to-end latency"), `target` (e.g. "under 5 s"),
`scope` (flows or C4 elements). Body: rationale, how it is measured, current value (linked to
the observability source, not copied).

#### Business rule (`business-rule`)

Additional front matter:
```yaml
scope: "RTP credit transfers, outbound"
effective_from: 2026-03-01
effective_to:                # set when a scheme change retires it
rule_source: policy          # policy | regulation | scheme-rule | product-decision | contract
```
Body sections:
1. **Rule** — one or two precise sentences. Use EARS style where it helps: "When `<trigger>`, the system shall `<response>`."
2. **Rationale** — why the rule exists.
3. **Exceptions** — explicit and exhaustive, or "none".
4. **Examples** — synthetic only.
5. **Verification** — tests or controls that prove it (`relations.verified_by_tests`).

#### ADR (`adr`)

MADR-aligned. Additional front matter:
```yaml
decision_date: 2026-05-14
deciders: [team:payments-hub, role:chief-architect]
```
Body sections: Context and problem · Decision drivers · Considered options · Decision ·
Consequences (positive, negative, follow-ups) · Compliance or risk impact · Links.

ADRs are immutable once `active` (accepted). Only `status`, `superseded_by` and `review_by`
may change afterwards. A new decision creates a new ADR with `supersedes`.

#### Capability (`capability`)

Body: purpose, actors, inputs/outputs at business level, rails and message types involved
(by domain ID), boundaries, related rules and components.

#### Glossary term (`glossary-term`)

Additional: `synonyms`, `not_to_be_confused_with`, `domain_term` (the domain `TERM-PAY-*`
this narrows, if any). A product defines a term only when it genuinely differs from the domain term.

#### Runbook (`runbook`)

Additional: `trigger`, `severity`, `systems` (catalog refs). Body: detection, diagnosis steps,
recovery steps, reconciliation after recovery, escalation, verification. Commands must be
tested; no secrets or production identifiers.

#### Obligation (`obligation`, domain tier)

Additional: `authority` (e.g. Federal Reserve, Nacha, The Clearing House, FinCEN, OFAC),
`instrument` (regulation, operating circular or rules document and section),
`applies_to_rails`, `effective_from`, `effective_to`, `grc_ref` (ID in the bank's GRC system).
Body: plain-language summary of the obligation in your own words, what it requires of systems,
evidence expected. Do not paste scheme rule text; link to the licensed source.

#### Control (`control`, domain tier)

Usually a pointer: `grc_ref`, `control_type` (preventive | detective), `automated` (bool),
`evidence`. The GRC system stays authoritative.

### 4. Relation vocabulary

Use only these keys under `relations:`. Values are lists of IDs or catalog refs.

| Key | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `implements` | this artifact realizes a capability or requirement |
| `governed_by` | this is constrained by an obligation, policy or rule |
| `applies_to` | components, APIs or systems the artifact constrains |
| `decided_in` | the ADR that made this so |
| `depends_on` | knowledge or component dependency |
| `verified_by_tests` | test paths or test IDs |
| `evidenced_by` | control evidence, review records |
| `related_sdlc` | SDLC artifacts (epic, PRD, spec) that introduced or changed it |
| `affects` | pain point → journeys, use cases or personas it hurts |
| `involves` | journey or use case → personas taking part |

Do not add `related_to`. If no typed relation fits, the link is probably not worth keeping.

### 5. Status lifecycle

```
proposed ──approve──> active ──> deprecated ──> retired
                        │
                        └──replace──> superseded (superseded_by: <new id>)
```

- Only a CODEOWNER review moves `proposed` to `active`.
- `superseded` requires `superseded_by` pointing to an existing, non-retired artifact.
- Agents read `active` by default. `proposed` may be read with an explicit caveat.

### 6. Review cadence defaults

| Type | Default `review_by` | Also review when |
|---|---|---|
| Business rule | 12 months | Scheme or policy change, related incident |
| Obligation | 12 months or scheme release cycle | Any rulebook, circular or regulation update |
| ADR | none (immutable); 24 months relevance check | Architecture change touching it |
| Capability | 12 months | Scope change |
| Architecture narrative | 6 months | Any container or integration change |
| Runbook | 6 months | After every use in an incident |
| Glossary term | 24 months | Conflict found |
| Persona, journey, use case | 12 months | New research, channel change, go-live of a target journey |
| Pain point | 6 months while open | New evidence; epic delivered |
| Quality attribute | 12 months | Incident, capacity change, new scheme requirement |

### 7. product.yaml

See `templates/product.yaml`. Required keys: `id`, `name`, `owner`, `lifecycle`,
`domain_context` (repo and pinned version), `architecture` (model folder and pinned model-format version),
`sdlc.framework`, `sdlc.artifact_locations`, `context_locations`, `systems_of_record`
(where live facts come from).

## Reference: SDLC Framework Integration (BMAD first, then others)

The product knowledge base never replaces the framework. It gives the framework a trusted
baseline to read, and receives durable knowledge back through promotion.

BMAD changes quickly (the v6 line has consolidated and renamed several skills and workflows
during 2026). Before configuring anything, check the installed version under `_bmad/` and
the release notes, and map by **artifact role**, not by workflow name.

### 1. BMAD artifact map

| BMAD artifact (role) | Typical location | Classification | Reads from baseline | Gives back to baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Configuration, agents, workflows | `_bmad/` | Framework, not knowledge | — | — |
| Product brief, PRD | `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/` | Delta | Overview, `PER-*`, `JRN-*`, open `PAIN-*`, `UC-*`, `CAP-*`, `BR-*`, `NFR-*`, domain obligations | Candidate use cases, capabilities, rules; target journeys; pain points marked planned |
| UX design | `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/` | Delta | Capabilities, glossary | Rarely; glossary terms |
| Architecture document | `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/` | Delta (change design) | Current and target C4 model, active ADRs, NFRs, domain patterns | A proposed interim or target model plus ADRs |
| Epics and stories | planning and implementation artifacts | Delta | Rule and ADR IDs cited in acceptance criteria | Links (`related_sdlc`) only |
| Sprint status | `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/` | Live state of the change | — | Never |
| Project context (AGENTS.md block in current releases; `project-context.md` in earlier v6) | `AGENTS.md` or `_bmad-output/` | Always-on instructions | Must not contradict baseline | — |
| Retrospective | per epic | Promotion trigger | — | Runs Mode D |
| Test design / traceability (Test Architect module, if used) | per epic | Delta plus evidence | `BR-*` IDs | `verified_by_tests` links |

### 2. Rules for BMAD products

1. **The baseline is the input, not the output.** Configure BMAD so the PM, architect and
   developer roles load `product.yaml`, `product-context/INDEX.md`, the active ADR list and
   relevant domain obligations at the start of planning. Use BMAD's supported customization
   mechanism for the installed version (agent customization files, workflow configuration,
   or a custom module). Do not edit BMAD core files; upgrades overwrite them.
2. **Cite IDs, don't restate.** PRDs, architecture docs and stories reference `BR-*`, `ADR-*`,
   `OBL-*` and `CAP-*` by ID. Restating a rule's text inside a story creates a second copy that drifts.
3. **Architecture document is a change design, expressed as architecture states.**
   - Greenfield: the accepted architecture becomes `target.architecture.json` (plus ADRs) at the
     readiness gate, and `current.architecture.json` at first go-live.
   - Brownfield / modernization: capture `current.architecture.json` first (Mode B). Each BMAD
     architecture document proposes the next `transition-NN.architecture.json` (and target
     changes via ADR). At go-live the delivered transition becomes current.
4. **Add a baseline check to the readiness gate.** Before implementation starts, verify the plan
   does not contradict active ADRs, active business rules or domain obligations, and that the
   proposed architecture model passes validation against its domain patterns (`calm validate`). Contradictions
   need a new ADR (superseding) or a plan change, decided by humans.
5. **Promote at the retrospective.** The epic retrospective is the natural gate for Mode D.
   Output: a promotion PR, or an explicit "no promotable knowledge" note.
6. **Archive completed deltas.** BMAD's own guidance warns that completed epics and stories left
   in planning or implementation folders get treated as current requirements. After promotion,
   move them to an archive location that agents do not search by default.
7. **Coexist in AGENTS.md.** Current BMAD releases maintain a verified project-context block in
   `AGENTS.md`. Keep it inside its own markers; the product-context block sits beside it.
   Neither tool edits the other's block.
8. **Do not use generated documentation dumps as baseline.** Both BMAD's current direction and
   independent research moved away from large generated repository overviews for agent context.
   If a code-to-docs generator is used for brownfield discovery, treat its output as evidence
   for drafting `proposed` artifacts, not as the baseline itself.

### 3. Modernization specifics

Modernization is the near-term priority and the riskiest case, because the legacy system's
behaviour is often the only specification.

- Extract business rules from legacy code and documents as `proposed` with `provenance.method:
  extracted` and evidence (program, paragraph or module, test case). Business and operations
  owners verify them before they become `active`.
- Record behavioural equivalence decisions explicitly as ADRs (what will intentionally differ in
  the new platform, and why).
- Keep `current`, `transition-NN` and `target` model files with `states.yaml` (format: `calm-conventions.md`).
  Each transition becomes current only when its slice goes live and its exit criteria are met.
- Parallel-run and reconciliation results are evidence (`evidenced_by`) for the rules they prove.

### 4. Other frameworks (generic mapping)

| Framework | Delta (framework-owned) | Potential overlap with baseline | Resolution |
|---|---|---|---|
| GitHub Spec Kit | `specs/NNN-*/spec.md`, `plan.md`, `tasks.md` | `.specify/memory/constitution.md` | Constitution references enterprise and domain standards by ID and adds only project-specific principles |
| OpenSpec | `openspec/changes/` | `openspec/specs/` is itself a current-behaviour baseline | Treat `openspec/specs/` as the authoritative behaviour spec; `product.yaml` points to it; do not duplicate into `product-context/` |
| Kiro | `.kiro/specs/` | `.kiro/steering/` | Steering files point to `AGENTS.md` and IDs; no restated rules |
| Scrum / Jira-only | Jira epics and stories | Confluence pages | Jira stays delta; durable Confluence content migrates to the baseline or is linked as `provenance.sources` |

In every case, record the mapping under `sdlc:` in `product.yaml` so agents can find both
the delta and the baseline.

## Reference: Payments Domain Profile

Knowledge in this file belongs in the **payments domain-context repository**, shared by every
product and referenced by ID and pinned version. Products do not copy it.

Compliance, legal and the bank's GRC system remain authoritative for obligations and controls.
The domain repo holds an engineering-oriented summary in its own words plus references. It is
not legal advice and must be validated with compliance owners.

### 1. What the domain tier should contain

| Area | Content | Authoritative source | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Rails | Per rail: purpose, participants, message set, settlement model, operating hours model, limits model, return/recall model | Scheme rulebooks, operating circulars | Store the model and references; operational values (actual cut-off times, limits) come from configuration or the system of record |
| Message catalog | Message types and versions in use per rail, usage guidelines in force | Scheme rulebooks and usage guidelines | Versions pinned per rail; scheme standards releases are change events |
| Mappings | Internal canonical payment model ↔ each rail's message formats, field-level rules | Domain repo (owned by domain architects) | Machine-readable (YAML/CSV) plus tests; a high-value, frequently reused asset |
| Code sets | Status reasons, return reasons (e.g. Nacha return codes, scheme reason codes), rejection reasons with internal meaning and handling | External code set publications + internal handling rules | Record internal handling as `BR-PAY-*` |
| Calendars and cut-offs | Definitions and where to get current values | Calendar service / configuration | Never hard-code dates in prose |
| Obligation register | `OBL-PAY-*` entries | GRC system | See section 2 |
| Controls | `CTL-PAY-*` pointers | GRC system | Link to evidence, not copies |
| Patterns | `PAT-PAY-*`: idempotency and duplicate detection, end-to-end tracking IDs (e.g. UETR), saga/compensation, funds control, sanctions screening placement, exception/repair queues, reconciliation, cut-over and parallel run | Domain ADRs | Each pattern names its ADR |
| Glossary | `TERM-PAY-*` | Domain repo | Products narrow, never redefine silently |

### 2. Obligation register seed (verify with compliance)

Typical instruments a US payments department maps. Record each as an `OBL-PAY-*` artifact with
`authority`, `instrument` and `grc_ref`, summarizing systems impact in your own words.

| Area | Instruments to consider |
|---|---|
| Fedwire Funds | Regulation J (12 CFR 210, subpart B), UCC Article 4A, Federal Reserve Operating Circular 6 |
| FedNow | Regulation J (subpart C), Federal Reserve Operating Circular 8 |
| CHIPS | CHIPS Rules and Administrative Procedures, UCC Article 4A |
| RTP | The Clearing House RTP Operating Rules |
| ACH | Nacha Operating Rules, Federal Reserve Operating Circular 4 (FedACH), Regulation E for consumer entries |
| Consumer transfers | Regulation E (12 CFR 1005), including remittance transfer requirements where applicable |
| Cross-border / SWIFT | SWIFT rulebook and standards releases, SWIFT Customer Security Programme |
| Sanctions | OFAC regulations (31 CFR Chapter V) and bank sanctions policy |
| BSA/AML | Funds transfer recordkeeping and travel rule (31 CFR 1010.410), bank AML policy |
| Privacy and data | GLBA and bank data classification policy; PCI DSS only if card data is in scope |
| Operational resilience | Bank BCP/DR, third-party risk, and change-management policies (often SOX ITGC-relevant) |

Each obligation should link to:
- the business rules that implement it (`BR-*` with `governed_by: [OBL-...]`),
- the controls that evidence it (`CTL-*`),
- the products and components it applies to.

That chain is what lets an agent answer "what must not break if I change this?" and lets an
auditor follow rule → code → test → evidence.

### 3. Effective dating is mandatory

Payments rules change on scheme calendars (rulebook updates, standards releases, operating
circular revisions, migration deadlines). Every obligation and domain rule carries
`effective_from` and, when known, `effective_to`. Agents must evaluate rules against the date
the behaviour will be live, not today's date, when planning a change.

### 4. Starter domain skills (aim for 5 to 10 first)

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `message-change` | Adds or changes a message or field: checks catalog version, mapping, code sets, validation rules, tests, affected products |
| `new-business-rule` | Drafts a `BR-*` with EARS wording, scope, obligation links, tests, and routes to the owner |
| `adr-writer` | Drafts a MADR-style ADR with payments decision drivers (latency, finality, reconciliation, compliance) |
| `payments-change-impact` | Given a change, lists affected obligations, rules, rails, products and controls from the register |
| `idempotency-and-duplicate-review` | Reviews a design or PR against `PAT-PAY` idempotency and duplicate-detection patterns |
| `reconciliation-runbook` | Drafts or updates a reconciliation and recovery runbook for a flow |
| `legacy-rule-extraction` | For modernization: extracts candidate rules from legacy code with evidence, as `proposed` |

Your organization's existing standards, security and governance skills stay in the enterprise
tier; domain skills build on them rather than repeating them.

### 5. Sensitive data rules for payments context

Never place in any tier: real account numbers, names, addresses, tax IDs, real transaction
IDs or UETRs from production, production message payloads, sanctions hit details, SAR-related
information, credentials, keys, certificates or internal hostnames marked restricted. Use
clearly synthetic examples (for example, reserved test routing numbers from scheme test
guides and obviously fake names).

## Reference: Governance and Controls

### 1. Ownership (RACI)

| Knowledge | Accountable | Approves changes | Consulted |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product Context standard, schemas, ID rules | Enterprise architecture | Architecture review board | Security, risk |
| AI usage and data-handling policy for context | CISO / AI governance | Policy owners | Legal, compliance |
| Domain obligations register | Domain architect + compliance liaison | Compliance | Legal, operations |
| Domain rules, mappings, patterns, glossary | Payments domain architects | Domain CODEOWNERS | Product architects |
| Personas, journeys, use cases, pain points | Product owner | Product CODEOWNERS (business) | UX research, operations, support |
| Product capabilities, business rules | Product owner | Product CODEOWNERS (business + architecture) | Operations |
| Quality attributes (NFRs) | Product architect | Product CODEOWNERS (architecture) | SRE, operations |
| Product architecture model, ADRs | Product architect | Product CODEOWNERS | Domain architects for pattern deviations |
| Runbooks | Product operations lead | Operations CODEOWNERS | SRE |
| Skills (any tier) | Tier owner | Tier CODEOWNERS + security review for scripts | Platform team |

Every `owner` value in front matter must resolve to a CODEOWNERS entry. Orphaned knowledge
is a quality-gate failure.

### 2. Approval and segregation of duties

- Changes to `product-context/`, `architecture/decisions/`, `obligations/`, `rules/` and skills
  require CODEOWNER review through a pull request.
- An agent may author a PR. It may not approve it, and the human who prompted the agent should
  not be the sole approver for rule, obligation or ADR changes.
- `status: proposed` → `active` happens only in a reviewed commit. The validator rejects
  `active` artifacts whose provenance is `ai-draft` or `extracted` without `verified_by`.
- Git history is the audit trail. Do not squash away review evidence for these folders.

### 3. Data handling

- Classify every artifact. `restricted` content does not enter the context layer; link to the
  controlled system instead, and let the agent retrieve it only through an entitled MCP/API call.
- Search and RAG indexes inherit the access controls of their sources. An index that lets a
  user retrieve content they could not open directly is a data-leak path.
- Secrets scanning and sensitive-data scanning run on context repos exactly as on code.
- Agent memory and chat transcripts are not a place to store product knowledge. Anything worth
  keeping goes through promotion.

### 4. Skill supply chain

Independent audits in 2026 found prompt injection in a large share of publicly shared skills.
Treat skills like code dependencies:

- Only install skills from the enterprise or domain tier, or from vetted sources pinned by version.
- Review `scripts/` and any network or shell access in every skill before approval.
- Record each skill in the catalog with owner, lifecycle and source location (Backstage supports
  an `AiResource` kind for skills and rules, and an `mcp-server` API type).
- Re-review on every version change.

### 5. MCP servers

- Register approved MCP servers in the catalog with owner, scopes and data classification.
- Prefer read-only scopes for context retrieval; write actions need their own approval path.
- Use per-user identity so entitlements and audit logs reflect the real requester.

### 6. Regulatory touchpoints to align with (confirm with risk and compliance)

- **Change management / SOX ITGC**: agent-authored changes follow the same review, approval and
  evidence rules as human changes.
- **Model risk management**: if agents make or materially support decisions in production
  processes, coordinate with the bank's model risk function (US banks commonly follow SR 11-7 /
  OCC 2011-12 style guidance). Design-time coding agents usually fall under software change
  controls, but confirm the classification.
- **Records retention**: ADRs, obligations and promotion PRs may be records; follow the retention schedule.
- **Third-party risk**: AI vendors and hosted MCP servers go through vendor risk review.

### 7. Conflict handling

When the validator, a review or an agent finds conflicting sources:
1. Apply the precedence order in `SKILL.md`.
2. Open an issue labelled `context-conflict`, owned by the accountable owner of the higher-precedence artifact.
3. Agents working on the affected area must cite the conflict and not silently choose.

---

## Reference: Retrieval, Catalog and Graph

Four mechanisms, each for a different question. Do not collapse them into one technology.

| Mechanism | Question it answers | Source of truth? |
|---|---|---|
| Files in Git (Markdown + front matter, contracts, model) | What do we know and why? | Yes, for durable knowledge |
| Catalog (e.g. Backstage) | What exists, who owns it, what depends on what? | Yes, only for metadata it is designated to own; otherwise an aggregator |
| Graph | How are things related across products and tiers? | No. Derived. |
| Search / RAG index | Where is the relevant unstructured material? | No. Derived. |
| MCP / APIs | What is true right now, and what can I do? | Proxies the system of record |

### 1. Retrieval order for agents

1. **Orient**: `AGENTS.md` → `product.yaml` → generated `product-context/INDEX.md`.
2. **Exact lookup**: follow IDs and paths (rules, ADRs, obligations, contracts). Coding agents
   are good at agentic file search; a clean ID scheme plus an index beats embedding search for
   authoritative content.
3. **Structured queries**: catalog or graph for ownership, dependencies, consumers.
4. **Live state**: MCP/API for deployments, incidents, tickets, runtime topology.
5. **Semantic search**: only for large unstructured history (old designs, post-mortems,
   Confluence archives). Results are treated as leads, then confirmed against authoritative files.
6. **Assemble minimal context**: include what the task needs; cite IDs.

The original plan's "classify task → graph traversal → retrieve" pipeline is a reasonable end
state for a central platform, but most value arrives earlier from steps 1 to 4. Build the
pipeline only when evaluation shows agents failing to find cross-product context.

### 2. When to introduce each component

| Component | Introduce when | Not before |
|---|---|---|
| Front matter + validator + INDEX.md | Day one | — |
| Domain-context repo | Two or more products share rules or mappings | — |
| Catalog descriptors (`catalog-info.yaml`) | The org runs a catalog, or products need cross-repo ownership lookup | — |
| MCP servers for Jira/Git/CI/observability/catalog | Agents need live state; approved servers exist | Security review done |
| Graph schema (node types, edge vocabulary, ID rules) | Day one | — |
| Graph v0 (JSON built by the validator in CI) | First product baseline exists | — |
| Graph database | Multi-hop golden questions fail on graph v0, more than ~5 products onboarded, impact analysis becomes a change-approval step, or runtime topology must join design-time data | Front matter and architecture models are consistent and validated across products |
| Semantic index | Unstructured archives are large and searched often | Access controls on the index match the sources |

### 3. Building the graph

- Graph v0: `validate_context.py --graph-out graph.json` emits nodes and typed edges from front
  matter `relations` and the architecture model (elements, relationships, flows, controls, linked IDs).
- Extract deterministically from: architecture model files (all states, tagged by state), front
  matter `relations`, `product.yaml`, catalog descriptors, OpenAPI/AsyncAPI, IaC and deployment manifests.
- LLM extraction is allowed only to propose edges; proposals are reviewed like any other artifact.
- Every edge carries provenance: source path or system, extraction method, extracted-at time,
  source commit or version.
- Rebuild on merge. Never edit the graph by hand. If a relationship is wrong, fix the source.
- Keep three logical layers: product (within one product), enterprise (across products, domains,
  teams), runtime (deployments and live dependencies, refreshed from systems of record).
- Model only relationships that answer real questions. Thousands of low-value edges make traversal noisy.

### 4. Architecture as code

- Architecture is described with the C4 model, stored as one model per state in the department format
  (FINOS CALM, see `calm-conventions.md`). C4 diagrams are generated views.
- Diagrams are generated views. Mermaid or PlantUML may be used for sequence and flow diagrams
  that the model does not cover, stored as source, rendered in CI.
- Architecture as code (structure, relationships, constraints, intent) is distinct from
  infrastructure as code (executable configuration). Link them; do not merge them.
- Fitness functions in CI can check the code against the model and ADRs (for example, forbidden
  dependencies, required idempotency middleware). These are the strongest drift detectors.

## Reference: Quality, Evaluation and Rollout

### 1. Assessment scorecard (Mode A / Mode E)

Score each dimension 0 to 3 (0 absent, 1 ad hoc, 2 defined, 3 enforced in CI or process).

| Dimension | 3 looks like |
|---|---|
| Identity | `product.yaml` complete, domain version pinned, catalog entry exists |
| Baseline coverage | Capabilities, rules, architecture model, ADRs and runbooks exist for all critical flows |
| Single source | No duplicated rules or architecture copies; SDLC artifacts cite IDs |
| Ownership | Every artifact owner resolves to CODEOWNERS |
| Freshness | No overdue `review_by` on active artifacts in critical flows |
| Provenance | AI-drafted or extracted artifacts are verified before activation |
| Traceability | Obligation → rule → component → test chain exists for regulated flows |
| Promotion loop | Every closed epic has a promotion PR or explicit "none" note |
| Agent usability | `AGENTS.md` within budget, commands verified, golden-set score tracked |
| Safety | No sensitive data findings; skills and MCP servers approved |

Report blockers first, then the three to five actions with the highest expected effect on the
golden-set score.

### 2. CI gates (knowledge as code)

Run on every PR that touches context folders:

| Check | Tool | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Front matter schema, required fields, enums | `scripts/validate_context.py` | Error |
| Unique IDs, ID format, file name matches ID | validator | Error |
| Supersession integrity (`superseded` needs a valid `superseded_by`) | validator | Error |
| Relations point to known IDs (product + domain) | validator | Error for rules/ADRs, warning otherwise |
| AI-drafted or extracted artifacts active without `verified_by` | validator | Error |
| `restricted` classification present | validator | Error |
| Overdue `review_by` | validator | Warning (error for obligations) |
| `AGENTS.md` over line budget | validator | Warning |
| INDEX.md regenerated | validator `--write-index` | Error if stale |
| Secrets / sensitive data scan | existing bank scanners | Error |
| Link check, diagram render | standard tools | Warning |
| Architecture fitness functions | ArchUnit or equivalent | Error for accepted-ADR violations |

### 3. Golden question set (Mode F)

`evaluation/golden-questions.yaml`:

```yaml
product: PMTHUB
version: 1
questions:
  - id: GQ-001
    task: "Add support for an additional status reason on outbound RTP rejects."
    category: change-impact        # lookup | change-impact | design | troubleshooting | compliance
    expected_sources: [BR-PMTHUB-042, OBL-PAY-011, messages/code-sets/status-reasons.yaml]
    expected_facts:
      - "Reject handling must follow BR-PMTHUB-042"
      - "Mapping lives in the domain repo, not the product"
    must_not_use: [BR-PMTHUB-017]  # superseded
  - id: GQ-002
    task: "Who approves a change to the reconciliation cut-off logic?"
    category: lookup
    expected_sources: [product.yaml, CODEOWNERS]
```

Aim for 20 to 40 questions per product across categories, written by engineers from real
tickets and incidents. Include questions whose correct answer is "this is not documented".

### 4. Metrics

| Metric | Definition | Starting target |
|---|---|---|
| Retrieval accuracy | Share of questions where every expected source was cited | ≥ 80% |
| Answer correctness | Share with all expected facts right (human or rubric graded) | ≥ 80% |
| Stale-source hits | Share citing superseded/deprecated artifacts without caveat | ≤ 2% |
| Decision adherence | Sampled agent designs/PRs that respect active ADRs and rules | ≥ 95% |
| Promotion coverage | Closed epics with promotion PR or "none" note | 100% |
| Duplication | Conflicting-source issues open | Trending down |
| Freshness | Active artifacts past `review_by` in critical flows | 0 |
| Rework | Review comments citing missing or wrong context (sampled) | Trending down |

Document count and page count are not success measures.

### 5. Rollout phases (summary)

The full implementation plan is maintained separately. Summary:

| Phase | Scope | Exit criteria |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Mobilize | Approve standard and architecture model format, define graph schema v1, pick 2 pilots, set up repos | Standard and schema approved |
| 1. Assess and measure | Mode A on pilots; golden questions; baseline score | Baseline recorded |
| 2. Domain tier seed | Glossary, message catalog, code sets, obligations, controls, 2-3 patterns | Domain v0.1 released and pinned |
| 3. Product baselines | Mode B: product.yaml, overview, personas, journeys, pain points, rules, current C4 model (+ interim/target where migrating), ADRs, runbooks; graph v0 in CI | Validator and model validation clean; score improved |
| 4. SDLC wiring | BMAD and non-BMAD touchpoints: read baseline, readiness check, promotion, go-live state update | First promotion and state update merged |
| 5. Skills and MCP | 5-10 skills; read-only MCP for Jira, Confluence, Git, SonarQube, catalog; graph query tool | Live-state and multi-hop questions pass |
| 6. Evaluate and decide | Re-score; go/no-go; graph database decision | Scale-out approved |
| 7. Scale out | Waves of 3-5 products; department landscape; enterprise graph | Department scorecard published |

## Reference: CALM Conventions (payments department)

FINOS CALM is the department's architecture model. These conventions keep models consistent
across products so they can be validated, compared across states, and joined with the rest of
the knowledge base. Pin the CALM schema version in `product.yaml` (`architecture.calm_schema`)
and upgrade deliberately.

### 1. Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `architecture/model/current.architecture.json` | As-is production architecture (always present) |
| `architecture/model/transition-NN.architecture.json` | Interim states, numbered in delivery order |
| `architecture/model/target.architecture.json` | Approved end state (omit when equal to current) |
| `architecture/model/states.yaml` | Ordered index of states (see section 7) |
| Domain repo `calm/patterns/*.pattern.json` | Approved patterns products validate against |
| Domain repo `calm/controls/CTL-PAY-*.requirement.json` | Control requirement definitions |
| Domain repo `calm/shared-nodes/*.json` | Shared systems (rails, sanctions screening, funds control) referenced by products |

### 2. Identity

- `unique-id` = catalog slug, lowercase kebab-case: `rtp-gateway` ↔ `component:rtp-gateway`.
- The same `unique-id` keeps its meaning in every state file. A replaced component gets a new ID; it is not renamed in place.
- Relationship IDs describe the interaction: `payment-api-screens-parties`, not `rel-1`.

### 3. Node types (C4 mapping)

| C4 concept | CALM `node-type` |
|---|---|
| Person | `actor` |
| Software system (ours or external) | `system` |
| Container: service, API, batch job, worker | `service` |
| Container: database, ledger store | `database` |
| Container: UI | `webclient` |
| Deployment environment, zone | `network`, `ecosystem` |
| Data set of note (e.g. payment ledger) | `data-asset` |

Structure with relationships: `composed-of` (system → containers → components), `connects`
(technical call or message, with `protocol`), `interacts` (actor → system), `deployed-in`
(node → environment). Model components only where they explain a decision or a control.

### 4. Metadata keys (use exactly these)

| Key | On | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `owner` | architecture, system, service | `team:<name>` from CODEOWNERS |
| `product` | architecture | product code (`PMTHUB`) |
| `classification` | node | `public`, `internal`, `confidential` |
| `business-rules` | node, relationship, flow | list of `BR-*` |
| `adrs` | any | list of `ADR-*` |
| `capabilities` | flow, system | list of `CAP-*` |
| `rails` | node, flow | domain rail IDs (`rtp`, `fedwire`, `fednow`, `ach`, `chips`, `swift`) |
| `messages` | relationship, interface | message types from the domain message catalog |
| `nfrs` | node, flow | list of `NFR-*` quality attributes the element must meet |
| `lifecycle` | node, relationship | `stable` (default), `transitional`, `retiring` |
| `sunset` | transitional elements | ISO date by which it must be gone |
| `data-tags` | node | `pii`, `npi`, `pci`, `sanctions-data` (drives controls and reviews) |

Values are IDs, never copied rule or policy text.

### 5. Controls

- Attach controls where they are enforced: the relationship (e.g. screening call), the node (e.g. encryption at rest), or the flow (e.g. dual authorization before release).
- `requirement-url` points to the domain control definition (`CTL-PAY-*`).
- `config` names the obligation and product settings: `{ "obligation": "OBL-PAY-020", "screening-point": "pre-release" }`.
- Every `data-tags` value implies required controls, defined in the domain patterns.

### 6. Flows

- One flow per critical payment journey: at least initiation, screening, funds control, release to rail, status handling, returns, repair.
- Transitions reference existing relationship IDs in sequence.
- Flow metadata lists `capabilities`, `business-rules` and `rails`.
- Flows replace hand-drawn sequence diagrams for these journeys; use Mermaid only for detail below the model's level.

### 7. States (`states.yaml`)

```yaml
product: PMTHUB
states:
  - id: current
    file: current.architecture.json
    status: live
    since: 2026-06-30
  - id: transition-01
    file: transition-01.architecture.json
    status: planned                 # planned | live | retired
    window: { from: 2026-11-15, to: 2027-03-31 }
    delivers: [EPIC-PMTHUB-12]      # SDLC references
    approved_by: [ADR-PMTHUB-031]
    exit_criteria:
      - "Parallel run shows zero unexplained reconciliation breaks for 20 business days"
  - id: target
    file: target.architecture.json
    status: planned
    approved_by: [ADR-PMTHUB-030]
```

- Exactly one `live` state, and its file is `current.architecture.json`.
- At go-live: copy the delivered state into `current.architecture.json`, mark it `live`, delete its transition file (Git keeps history), update `since`.
- Transitional elements whose `sunset` has passed fail CI.

### 8. CI and authoring

- **CI:** `calm validate` against the declared pattern(s); `validate_context.py` checks IDs inside CALM files, unique IDs, flow transitions and `states.yaml`; views regenerated (`calm docify` or the organization's renderer).
- **Authoring:** use the CALM VS Code extension and its AI assistant, or an agent with this skill; review the diff, not the JSON by hand. Start from `templates/architecture.json`.
- **Graph:** nodes and relationships are extracted directly into the knowledge graph; metadata IDs become edges to rules, ADRs, obligations and capabilities.

---

## Templates

Copy these into a product repository and fill the placeholders.

### AGENTS.md

````markdown
# AGENTS.md

<!-- BEGIN product-context (owner: product architect; keep this block under ~80 lines) -->
## Product
<Product name> (`<PRODUCT-ID>`): <one sentence on what it does and for whom>.
Identity, owners, dependencies and SDLC mapping: `product.yaml`.
Knowledge index (generated): `product-context/INDEX.md`.

## Commands (verified <YYYY-MM-DD>)
- Build: `<command>`
- Unit tests: `<command>`
- Integration tests: `<command>`
- Lint and context validation: `<command>` and `python <path>/validate_context.py --root .`

## Hard constraints
- Follow active ADRs in `architecture/decisions/` and active rules in `product-context/business-rules/`. If code contradicts them, stop and report the drift.
- Payments rules, message mappings, code sets and obligations come from the payments domain context `<repo>@<version>`. Reference them by ID; never copy them here.
- Never put real customer data, account numbers, production messages or secrets in code, tests, fixtures or docs. Use synthetic data.
- Live facts (deployed version, incidents, ticket status) come from MCP tools, not from docs.
- Every change must be idempotent-safe on payment paths; see `PAT-PAY-001`.

## Architecture
- C4 model in `architecture/model/`: `current.architecture.json` is what runs in production; `states.yaml` lists interim and target states.
- Users and problems: `product-context/personas/`, `journeys/`, `use-cases/`, `pain-points/`.
- Troubleshooting and operations: use current. Implementing a slice: diff current against the transition state it delivers. Design: use target.

## Where things go
- Changing behaviour? Work in the SDLC framework (`<e.g. _bmad-output/>`), cite `BR-*` / `ADR-*` IDs.
- Found a new durable rule or decision? Draft it as `status: proposed` and flag it for promotion; do not mark it active.

## Skills
Product skills: `.agents/skills/`. Domain and enterprise skills are installed from their repos.
<!-- END product-context -->

<!-- Other tools (for example BMAD's project-context block) keep their own marked sections below. -->
````

### product.yaml

```yaml
# product.yaml — identity and map of a product's context.
# Keys marked (required) are checked by validate_context.py.

id: PMTHUB                              # (required) product code used in artifact IDs
name: Payment Hub                       # (required)
description: Routes and processes outbound and inbound payments across US rails.
owner: team:payments-hub                # (required) must resolve in CODEOWNERS
lifecycle: production                   # (required) experimental | production | deprecated
business_unit: payments
catalog_ref: system:payment-hub         # catalog entity, if a catalog is used

domain_context:                         # (required) pinned shared knowledge
  repo: payments-domain-context
  version: 1.4.0

architecture:                           # (required)
  model: architecture/model/            # C4 model, one file per state, + states.yaml
  format: finos-calm                    # department model format
  format_version: <pinned version>
  patterns: [idempotent-intake, screen-before-release]   # domain patterns this product claims

enterprise_context:
  repo: enterprise-context
  version: 2.1.0

sdlc:                                   # (required)
  framework: bmad                       # bmad | spec-kit | openspec | kiro | scrum | other
  framework_version: "6.x"
  artifact_locations:
    planning: _bmad-output/planning-artifacts/
    implementation: _bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/
    archive: archive/sdlc/              # completed deltas, not searched by default
  promotion_gate: epic-retrospective

context_locations:                      # (required) where baseline knowledge lives
  capabilities: product-context/capabilities/
  business_rules: product-context/business-rules/
  glossary: product-context/glossary/
  architecture_model: architecture/model/
  decisions: architecture/decisions/
  operations: operations/
  skills: .agents/skills/
  evaluation: evaluation/golden-questions.yaml

contracts:
  - path: services/payment-api/openapi.yaml
    kind: openapi
  - path: services/payment-events/asyncapi.yaml
    kind: asyncapi

rails: [fedwire, rtp, fednow, ach]      # domain rail IDs this product uses

systems_of_record:                      # where live facts come from (via MCP/API)
  tickets: jira:PMTHUB
  deployments: <ci-cd system / project>
  incidents: <incident system / service id>
  ownership: <org directory or catalog>
  runtime: <observability system / service id>

depends_on:
  - system:sanctions-screening
  - system:funds-control
consumers:
  - system:treasury-portal
```

### states.yaml

```yaml
# states.yaml - ordered index of architecture states for one product.
# Exactly one state is "live" and its file is current.architecture.json.
product: PMTHUB
states:
  - id: current
    file: current.architecture.json
    status: live
    since: 2026-06-30

  # Interim state: remove this block and its file once it goes live.
  - id: transition-01
    file: transition-01.architecture.json
    status: planned                 # planned | live | retired
    window: { from: 2026-11-15, to: 2027-03-31 }
    delivers: [EPIC-PMTHUB-12]      # SDLC references (BMAD epic, Jira epic, spec)
    approved_by: [ADR-PMTHUB-031]
    exit_criteria:
      - "Parallel run shows zero unexplained reconciliation breaks for 20 business days"

  # Target state: omit when the target equals the current state.
  - id: target
    file: target.architecture.json
    status: planned
    approved_by: [ADR-PMTHUB-030]
```

### promotion-checklist.md

````markdown
# Knowledge Promotion — <epic / feature reference>

Use as the PR description for a promotion PR (Mode D).

## Source change
- SDLC artifacts: <PRD / epic / stories / spec paths or links>
- Merged code: <PR links>
- Incidents or review notes consulted: <links or "none">

## Candidates

| # | Kind | Proposed artifact | New or update | Evidence | Owner to approve |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | business rule | BR-<PRODUCT>-<NNN> | update v2 → v3 | <link> | team:<...> |
| 2 | decision | ADR-<PRODUCT>-<NNN> | new | <link> | team:<...> |

Or: **No promotable knowledge.** Reason: <e.g. change was purely internal refactoring>.

## Checks
- [ ] Searched for existing artifacts before creating new ones (no near-duplicates)
- [ ] Domain-level knowledge proposed to the domain repo, not copied here
- [ ] All new or changed artifacts are `status: proposed` with evidence in `provenance.sources`
- [ ] Superseded artifacts updated with `superseded_by`
- [ ] Contradictions with the baseline listed below
- [ ] No sensitive data; examples are synthetic
- [ ] `validate_context.py` passes and `INDEX.md` regenerated
- [ ] Completed SDLC artifacts ready to archive after merge

## Contradictions found
<List any conflicts with active rules, ADRs or obligations, or "None.">
````

## Validator

The CI validator ships with the skill as `scripts/validate_context.py` (Python 3.9+, PyYAML). Get it from the canonical skill repository.
